notes_for_editor: Newspapers (Chronicling America) were tried but returned nothing usable in the time allowed. Early history (1803-1852) rests on LighthouseFriends alone (copyrighted, paraphrased); no 1852 Light-House Board report was in the corpus. Roster from USLHS agrees with LighthouseFriends except William L. Lockhart 1951 (LF only). The 1891 dwelling rests on the NRHP and the owner's history, the 1891 report itself was not read. OCR names: schooner 'Vicksburgh' printed 'Yicksburgh'; 'Addie Ryerson' printed 'Ryarson'/'Ey arson'. Fiscal-year hours (2,243 = FY1891; 2,324 = FY1892; 2,272 = FY1894) taken from the report volumes by position. The Commissioner's Otter Island note gives a garbled end year for its '15 years' of accidents. The 1914 Bulletin item (Reed, 6 August) is placed in the 1914 volume; its year was not confirmed. Third-order lens year: 1855 (USLHS, LF) vs 1857 (Lighthouse Digest, New England Lighthouses). Pine Island Camp transfer: 1997 (owner, LF, LH Digest) vs 1996 (Wikipedia). Head keeper's dwelling built 1899 (LF) or 1900 (owner); Board reports show appropriation March 1899 and conversion in fiscal 1900. Abbie Burgess Grant's Matinicus Rock fame is only touched on; the USLHS record lists her Whitehead term as first assistant 1875-1890. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Otter Island estimate's '15 years preceding 1935' is a misprint (report is 1920); story says so. Lighthouse Digest lists grounds open, LighthouseFriends closed: story states the disagreement. Roster (USLHS) stops at 1952; LighthouseFriends also lists William L. Lockhart 1951 and later Coast Guard names, not used (living-people rule).
